hero.eyebrow: For care settings and employees' families in Taiwan
hero.h1:
For the hours no one can be there,
there is an AI that cares
hero.sub: A real face and a real voice, talking with your elders every day, covering the nights, the quiet hours and the distance that no team can staff. Usage and care outcomes are visible every month, so ESG teams and families both have something to show.
hero.note1: Start with a small pilot, expand once it works
hero.note2: Pure software, download and go, no implementation project
hero.chip1: Reminded Mom to take her medicine
hero.chip2: She remembers what you told her
stat.h2: Taiwan is now a super-aged society, and there aren't enough hands
stat.l1: 1 in every 5 people is an elder
stat.d1: Taiwan officially became a super-aged society in 2025
stat.l2: of care facilities are chronically short-staffed
stat.d2: One in four waits six months to fill a single caregiver role
stat.l3: The health cost of long-term loneliness
stat.d3: Research puts the risk on par with smoking 15 cigarettes a day
stat.l4: Annual growth in AI elder care
stat.d4: Global market estimated at US$67 billion in 2026

value.h2: Not one more chatbot, but the care gap finally filled
value.sub: What buyers actually purchase isn't AI vocabulary. It's a service elders will use, front-line staff can read at a glance, and families can feel.
value.pa: Long-term memory lets every conversation pick up where the last one ended: a sore knee, a grandchild's wedding, the old street they love to visit. She keeps it all. Familiarity is what makes an elder open the app a second and third time.
value.pb: In everyday conversation she picks up low mood and warning signs: a voice that sounds off, a mention of pain, something worrying said out loud. Family and caregivers are notified right away, so "something's not right" becomes "we knew early".
value.h3c: Peace of mind you can see
value.pc: Family open the app and see how Mom and Dad are doing today, their mood, and whether reminders were completed. Worry from far away finally has somewhere to go, instead of one phone call after another.
pain.h2: Start with who is accountable, who uses it, and who feels the value
pain.sub: A proposal that closes has to answer all four at once: the manager's staffing problem, the front line's workflow problem, whether elders will actually use it, and whether families feel reassured.
pain.h3a: Adult children worrying from another city
pain.a1: Mom and Dad are alone all day with no one to really talk to
pain.a2: You're not there, so you don't know how their day went
pain.a3: Medicine taken? Follow-up due? Reminders from a distance always arrive late
pain.b1: Rounds and reporting eat up most of a caregiver's day
pain.b2: Constant calls from families wear out the front desk
pain.b3: Nobody can fill the companionship gap at night and in the quiet hours
pain.h3c: The invisible load of employees caring for parents
pain.c1: Employees worry about parents far away: leave taken, focus lost, people hard to retain
pain.c2: The S in the sustainability report lacks anything concrete people can feel
pain.c3: The benefits budget is spent, and employees don't notice
pain.h3d: The differentiation problem in community services
pain.d1: Thin staffing at night and off-peak leaves companionship uncovered
pain.d2: Residents feel lonely, and belonging is hard to build
pain.d3: Competition for residents is fierce and services all look alike
pain.punch: A pilot isn't a technology showcase. It tests three things: whether elders want to talk, whether the front line does less duplicate work, and whether families feel more at ease.
proof.h2: A US state government ran AI companionship for elders for three years. It worked.
proof.sub: Since 2022 New York State has placed AI companions in the homes of elders living alone. From the official tracking:
proof.bar3: felt more connected to the world
proof.note1: Elders started conversations 30+ times a day, six days a week — nobody made them. They wanted to talk.
proof.note2: In 2025 alone 3,500 elders applied to join, and the state keeps expanding the program.
proof.note3: Munea is doing the same proven thing for Taiwan's elders: in Mandarin, with a real face and a real voice, remembering every single person.
proof.cite: Source: New York State Office for the Aging (NYSOFA) official program reports, 2022–2026
sol.eyebrow: Priority markets and ways to work together
sol.h2: Start where we're closest to the floor and easiest to verify
sol.sub: Phase one focuses on long-term and day care, senior living, and family care support for employers. Other partnerships are open once a pilot confirms the need.
sol.h3a: The hours you can't cover, covered first
sol.matha: Start with a small pilot and watch whether elders find it easy and whether families feel more at ease. We don't promise labor savings we haven't verified.
sol.a1: Families check in through the app: watch whether inquiries drop and reassurance rises
sol.a2: Care signals, organized: your team defines together which situations need a human
sol.h3b: Turn family care support into a benefit employees actually use
sol.mathb: Start with a small group of employees' parents and see whether it's easy to use and whether the caregiving pressure eases. ESG reporting only ever sees anonymous totals; individual health and conversations are never handed to the company.
sol.b1: A companion of their own for employees' elders: the company provides the seats, and employees' parents have Munea with them
sol.b2: Linked family app: employees can check on their parents any time
sol.b3: 10 accounts or more include a monthly results report: usage・care・exception summary
sol.priceb: / person · month・NT$100 less per seat than the App Store price
sol.h3c: "A community that cares" is the next reason people move in
sol.mathc: Someone to talk to in the room, no empty stretch at night or off-peak, and residents are more willing to stay. Keeping one extra household for a year far outweighs a whole floor's annual seat fees.
sol.c1: A companion for each resident: she remembers everyone, and gets more familiar over time
sol.c2: Nights and off-peak covered: companionship continues when staffing is thin
sol.c3: A reason to choose you: something visitors can see and you can talk about
sol.pricec: / unit · month (benchmarked to facility seats, agreed by scale)
sol.h3d: Care as the add-on that keeps members
sol.mathd: Follow-up reminders that land mean return visits; members who feel remembered renew. Care add-ons are the hardest kind of differentiation to price-shop.
sol.d1: Health education, delivered warmly: care knowledge shared through conversation
sol.d2: Follow-up and medication reminders: spoken out loud on time, never missed
sol.d3: Member service that stands apart: others sell products; you offer a care companion
sol.h3e: Add Munea to your service line-up and open a new revenue share
sol.mathe: Add value for the clients you already have without building a product team: channel revenue share, joint offerings, and pilot-site partnerships are all open to discussion.
sol.pricee: Revenue share and joint marketing, by agreement
gal.h2: What elders see is exactly this simple
gal.sub: Big type, few buttons, just start talking. Every screen is designed for an elder's fingers and eyes.
gal.cap1: Home: today's companionship starts with a hello
gal.cap2: Live conversation: a real face and voice, as natural as a video call
gal.cap3: Health: medication, mood and activity at a glance
gal.cap4: Family circle: relatives see how their elder is doing, as it happens
gal.cap5: Settings: reminders and preferences, tuned to suit them
tech.h2: Staff go home at the end of a shift. Care doesn't.
tech.sub: A real face and voice, an ear for how Taiwan's elders actually speak, and memory of every conversation — the three foundations that let her keep showing up.
tech.pText: Real-time voice and face bring the interaction to life, and the character, the boundaries of care, Traditional Chinese for Taiwan and the family reporting flow all live in one experience. We don't ask you to buy on claims of being "first" or "ahead" that we can't prove.
tech.demoCap: See for yourself・turn the sound on
tech.vhint1: Turn the sound on and hear how her voice lines up with her expression
tech.vhint2: The same engine, a different companion
tech.a1: A real human face, generated live, that speaks and shows expression
tech.a2: She understands and answers back, and you can cut in any time
tech.a3: Face and voice in sync, mouth movement following the sound
tech.a4: Traditional Chinese for Taiwan, tuned to how people here actually speak
tech.a5: Tone follows feeling: when you're tired, she softens
tech.b1: She remembers what was said, growing more familiar over time
tech.b2: Medication and follow-up reminders, spoken out loud on time
tech.b3: Mood and anomaly awareness, hearing when something is off
tech.b4: Family and caregivers notified right away, so help is called when it matters
tech.b5: A family health circle, where everyone's status is visible
tech.h3c: The foundation holding it all steady
tech.c1: Our own real-time voice and video engine, so she feels present
tech.c2: A care-focused intelligence core that understands elders and knows where the line is
tech.c3: Cloud service architecture, with capacity and network verified to the pilot's scale
tech.c4: Security and personal data protection: data serves care, nothing else
tech.c5: Medical boundaries held: no diagnosis, medication reminders only
tech.closeTag: Why we call her "the whole family's AI health companion and care assistant"
tech.closeText: The interaction layer makes elders want to talk, the care layer turns every sentence into protection, and the technology layer keeps it all running steadily. Together they add up to one assistant who remembers every elder, who can see and hear, and who calls for help when something happens.
demo.h2: See for yourself. Talk to Ningning directly.
demo.sub: Not a video, not a text chat. Once unlocked you go straight into a 3-minute real face and voice session, using only your microphone and your voice.
demo.lockP: The passphrase is in our invitation message. Don't have one? Use "Book a 30-minute consultation" at the top right and we'll walk you through the whole thing ourselves.
demo.lead: This is an isolated guest session: no sign-in, no real user memory or health data, no reminders created. Please use Chrome or Safari and allow microphone access; waking the video service for the first time can take a moment. The demo is conducted in Traditional Chinese (Taiwanese Mandarin).
price.h2: Seat-based. You pay for what you use.
price.sub: A pure software subscription: employees download the app and start. No build-out, no implementation project. Buying in bulk, each corporate seat costs NT$100 less than the App Store price (Plus 599→499, Pro 1199→1099); 10 accounts or more include a monthly results report, and quarterly or analytical reports are a paid option. The figures below are reference starting points and don't imply unlimited calling.

policy.h2: 2026 is a big year for care technology policy in Taiwan
policy.sub: Public funding that can go alongside adopting Munea:
policy.li1: Residential facility quality incentive program (2024–2027): backed by the Ministry of Health and Welfare's long-term care fund, with a "smart assistive care technology" indicator. Adopting a smart care solution can be written into your indicator plan, and we help prepare the paperwork.
policy.li2: Long-term Care 3.0 smart assistive device rental benefit (effective July 2026): NT$60,000 of rental allowance per care household every three years. Munea's application is in planning (a plan under review, not an established benefit item); if included, the cost to families should drop substantially.
policy.punch: Our principle: subsidies are a bonus, not a precondition. The value has to stand on its own first — hours given back to staff, reassurance for families, something employees actually feel. Subsidies just make the decision easier.
steps.sub: We don't ask for a big contract up front: see it, try it, and only convert once it meets the targets.
steps.pa: Online or on site, talk with Munea yourself and see how she remembers people and holds emotion.
steps.pb: We learn your participants, language and network conditions, and deliver a pilot plan for you within two weeks.
steps.pc: Start with 10–20 participants and review weekly: how easily it's used, what families say, and where a human had to step in.
steps.pd: Against the targets agreed in advance, decide to expand, adjust or stop. Final pricing and scope of responsibility are confirmed in the contract.
promise.h2: Care settings deserve an honest partner
promise.pa: Munea is an assistive care and reminder tool. It does not replace human care or emergency medical judgment, and it does not provide diagnosis or medical advice. The escalation flow and responsibilities for warning signs are defined explicitly in the contract.
promise.pb: Elders' conversations and health data are collected and processed under Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act, with consent forms, data processing agreements, retention limits and purpose limitation all in place. Data is never used for anything outside the service.
promise.pc: The service runs primarily in Mandarin, tuned to how people in Taiwan speak. Taiwanese Hokkien is still being improved, and we can assess your setting's language needs before rollout. Other languages are not supported today.
final.quote:
Everyone is teaching AI to answer questions.
We chose to teach AI to care.
final.sub: See it, try it, expand once it works.
